text: Why do some people earn more every year, and still have nothing?
Three men fish the same river. Every evening, each one carries home one full basket.
The first man wants a new boat. Not next year. Now. So he borrows.
And every loan cuts a little hole in his basket.
He leaves the river with a full basket, and gets home with half.
So he fishes longer. Borrows again to cover the gap. More holes.
The holes don't care how hard he works.
The second man borrows nothing. Every night, one fish goes into a barrel. Slow. Safe. Boring.
The third man saves too. But when his barrel is full, he walks over to the first man.
Now every fish that falls through those holes lands in his basket.
Soon he has a basket under every hole in town.
One paid the interest. One avoided it. One collected it.
So if your basket has holes, someone is holding the basket underneath.
